question.problem: Expressed as an improper fraction in lowest terms, $\frac{1}{4}+3-\frac{5}{8}=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To evaluate this expression, we use PEMDAS.

We add and subtract, from left to right:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}+3-\frac{5}{8} & = \\ (\frac{1}{4}+3)-\frac{5}{8} & = \\ (\frac{1}{4}+\frac{12}{4})-\frac{5}{8} & = \\ \frac{1+12}{4}-\frac{5}{8} & = \\ \frac{13}{4}-\frac{5}{8} & = \\ \frac{26}{8}-\frac{5}{8} & = \\ \frac{26-5}{8} & = \\ \frac{21}{8}\end{aligned}
$$
